key_insight: The paper argues that robot policies should not depend on being told the camera pose at test time. Instead, the model learns to infer view changes on its own, enabling robust action prediction even when cameras are moved or remounted.
problem_solved: It addresses the fragility of Vision-Language-Action policies under camera repositioning and remounting. Existing view-robust methods typically need explicit camera extrinsics, which limits practicality in real-world deployment.
method: Introduces a calibration-free VLA framework that handles changing camera viewpoints without requiring provided extrinsic parameters.
Learns to infer camera/view information internally so the policy can remain robust across different placements.
Targets real-world robot settings where camera setup is unstable and may vary after deployment.
impact: This makes VLA policies easier to deploy in real robots because practitioners no longer need precise camera calibration for every setup. It improves robustness in dynamic environments where camera positions cannot be guaranteed.
